ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: This account is primarily rank-constrained in non-brand: the three in-scope non-brand search campaigns are capturing only 5–7% search impression share while losing 93–95% to rank with 0% lost to budget, despite only ~56–59% budget utilization. Auction evidence corroborates low placement (self top-of-page rate 15.2% vs competitors 73.2%) and indicates the bulk of missed volume is not being throttled by budget but by ad rank/position. Secondary waste is coming from competitor-brand, zero-click query leakage (35,700 impressions; 48.3% of search-term impressions) plus a small but fixable negative-keyword conflict blocking ~3,810 impressions.
notable_patterns: Non-brand search is almost entirely losing auctions on rank: Auto IS 6% with 94% lost rank; Home IS 5% with 95% lost rank; Life IS 7% with 93% lost rank, while all three show 0% lost to budget and only ~56–59% budget utilization.

Placement is materially worse than competitors: avg top-of-page rate is 15.2% for you vs 73.2% for competitors; avg outranking share is only 9.1%, and Nordkreuz is above you 96.5% of the time (top-of-page 82.6% vs your 17.1%).

High-quality keywords still have extremely low impression share (e.g., "auto insurance germany" QS 9.0 but IS 5% / 95% lost rank; "home insurance cost" QS 8.5 but IS 5.5% / 94.5% lost rank), pointing to bids/ad-rank thresholds rather than keyword quality being the limiting factor on those terms.

There is measurable spend concentration on low-quality, poor-efficiency queries/keywords (e.g., "insurance company phone number" QS 3.0, spend 2,605.80 with cost/conv 1,371.47; "home insurance claims process" QS 4.0, spend 2,248.95 with cost/conv 244.45), which is likely dragging overall ad rank and ROI while not solving the impression share problem.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Search impression share is only 6% with 94% lost to rank and 0% lost to budget while budget utilization is 57.2%, indicating bids/ad rank are the binding constraint rather than budget. ROAS is 0.7 (14,796.24 revenue on 21,070.38 spend), so scaling without fixing query mix and rank efficiency will amplify losses.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Restructure/segment intent, raise bids only on the highest-intent non-brand terms (especially QS 8–9 terms) to regain top-of-page share, and add/expand negatives to cut informational/job/competitor leakage that is consuming rank and spend.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Only 5% impression share with 95% lost to rank at 0% budget loss and 58.5% budget utilization; average quality score is weak (4.1), and ROAS is 0.75 (8,619.36 on 11,505.20), suggesting both rank pressure and relevance/landing-page alignment issues.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Tighten ad groups around quote/comparison intent, refresh RSAs/landing pages for core home-insurance themes to lift QS from ~4 toward 6+, and concentrate bids on converting intents while excluding claims-process/informational traffic.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Impression share is 7% with 93% lost to rank and 0% lost to budget at 56.2% budget utilization; average quality score is extremely low (2.0), which will materially suppress ad rank even at higher bids. ROAS is 0.89 (8,684.62 on 9,728.00), so there is room to improve efficiency before attempting scale.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Prioritize quality score recovery (keyword-to-ad-to-landing alignment) for life insurance, split informational terms from quote/comparison terms, and only bid up the segments that achieve acceptable CPA/ROAS once QS lifts.

recommendation_cards.title: Fix non-brand ad rank by bidding up only the high-intent, high-QS terms (and stop paying for low-intent drag)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Across non-brand search, impression share is 5–7% while 93–95% is lost to rank (Auto 94%, Home 95%, Life 93%) with 0% lost to budget and only ~56–59% budget utilization. Even your best keywords are barely entering auctions: "auto insurance germany" (QS 9.0) is at 5% IS with 95% lost rank; "car insurance quote" (QS 8.0) at 6% IS / 94% lost rank; "home insurance cost" (QS 8.5) at 5.5% IS / 94.5% lost rank.
recommended_steps: Create a dedicated high-intent segment (quote/comparison/buy-now) in each non-brand campaign and move the QS 7.5–9.0 keywords into it (e.g., "auto insurance germany", "car insurance quote", "life insurance comparison").
Increase bids/aggressiveness only in that segment until top-of-page rate improves, while holding or reducing bids on broad/informational clusters driving poor CPA.
Add strict intent negatives in the low-intent segments (e.g., "phone number", "claims", "what is") so spend doesn’t keep flowing to terms unlikely to convert.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Top-of-page rate for non-brand moving from ~15% account avg toward 25%+ while maintaining/improving ROAS (non-brand currently 0.7–0.89).

recommendation_cards.title: Recover Quality Score in Life Insurance first (QS 2.0 is a structural rank blocker)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Non-Brand Search - Life Insurance has avg quality score 2.0, 7% impression share, and 93% lost to rank with 0% lost to budget. This is consistent with auction pressure where competitors show far higher top-of-page presence (competitors 73.2% top-of-page rate vs your 15.2%).
recommended_steps: Split life insurance into separate ad groups for (a) comparison/quote intent and (b) informational education; ensure each group has tightly matched headlines/descriptions and a dedicated landing page section.
Pause or heavily downbid the worst informational terms that are consuming budget with poor efficiency (e.g., "what is life insurance" has QS 4.5 and cost/conv 613.56).
Rewrite the one 'Average' ad into an intent-matched variant for life insurance (comparison/quote language + clear price/benefit hooks) and align final URL to the exact product/quote path.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Life campaign avg QS rising from 2.0 toward 4.0+ and lost-to-rank dropping from 93% toward <85%.

recommendation_cards.title: Stop competitor-brand, zero-click leakage that is consuming nearly half of search-term impressions
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Competitor-brand zero-click impressions are 35,700, and 48.3% of search-term impressions are from zero-click competitor terms (e.g., "bluewave insurance", "harborline mutual", "crestfield direct"). Only one competitor-brand term is shown converting ("nordkreuz insurance quote" with 1.0 conversion), implying most of this volume is low-value and likely depresses efficiency and ad rank.
recommended_steps: Add competitor names as exact/phrase negatives in non-brand campaigns (start with Bluewave Insurance, Harborline Mutual, Crestfield Direct) while keeping a narrowly scoped exception only where you intentionally conquest and can prove ROI.
Create a separate, capped 'Competitor Conquest' campaign/ad group if conquesting is required; isolate budgets and measure it separately so it doesn’t pollute non-brand learning and QS.
Review search terms weekly for new competitor variants/misspellings and add them to the negative list.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Share of impressions from competitor-brand zero-click terms falling from 48.3% toward <15% without reducing conversions.

recommendation_cards.title: Eliminate the negative-keyword conflict blocking your own demand (3,810 impressions)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Two negative conflicts are blocking estimated 3,810 impressions: negative "free" blocks "insurance quote calculator free" in Dynamic Search Ads - Long Tail (3,400 blocked impressions), and negative "jobs" blocks "insurance agent jobs near me insurance quote" in Non-Brand Search - Auto Insurance (410 blocked impressions).
recommended_steps: In the negative-keyword conflicts report, change the "free" negative from broad/phrase to an exact-match negative for the truly unwanted variants (or move it to only the campaigns where it’s required), so you don’t block the intended long-tail keyword.
Keep "jobs" as a negative but add a more precise structure: exclude "jobs" in informational/job-hunting ad groups while ensuring quote-intent keywords aren’t trapped by broad negatives.
After resolving, monitor the previously blocked keyword(s) for conversion rate and add additional negatives if the traffic is low-intent.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impressions and conversions on the formerly blocked terms; target that the incremental traffic achieves at least the account’s non-brand average conversion rate (or pause again).

recommendation_cards.title: Cut/contain the worst-performing low-QS spend to fund rank recovery where it actually converts
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Several low-quality, high-cost keywords show extreme inefficiency: "insurance company phone number" (QS 3.0) spent 2,605.80 with cost/conv 1,371.47; "home insurance claims process" (QS 4.0) spent 2,248.95 with cost/conv 244.45. Meanwhile, the account is not budget-limited (0% lost to budget; ~52–58% budget utilization).
recommended_steps: Pause or sharply downbid the top 2–5 worst CPA keywords immediately (starting with "insurance company phone number" and "home insurance claims process"); add term-level negatives like "phone number" and "claims process" where appropriate.
Reallocate the freed spend into the segmented high-intent non-brand groups to improve top-of-page presence on QS 7.5–9 terms.
Re-check search terms after 3–5 days to ensure the waste does not re-enter via close variants/DSA expansions.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Non-brand cost/conv trending down (remove outliers first) while non-brand impression share increases above 6–7%.

already_working: Budget is not the limiting factor: all campaigns show 0% impression share lost to budget and only ~51–59% budget utilization (e.g., Auto 57.2%, Home 58.5%, Life 56.2%).
Brand is relatively healthy on coverage and efficiency: Brand Search - DE has 85% impression share with only 15% lost to rank and ROAS 4.7 (162,433.83 revenue on 34,552.32 spend).

Creative coverage is generally solid: 80% of ads are rated Good/Excellent (3 Excellent, 1 Good out of 5), so the biggest near-term lever is rank/targeting rather than a broad ad rewrite across the whole account.

market_mapping.why_now_summary: You’re leaving substantial non-brand demand uncaptured because performance is structurally rank-constrained (not budget-constrained) at the same time the German insurance search market is heating up. With only 9.02% impression share and 91.0% lost to rank (0.0% lost to budget), incremental budget alone won’t unlock volume—improving ad rank (bids focused on high-intent + Quality Score) and removing low-value/irrelevant leakage is the fastest path to regain share. External benchmarks reinforce that the “normal” insurance advertiser in Germany is achieving materially higher coverage (21.0% vertical-average impression share) while category spend is growing quickly (18.0% QoQ), meaning the opportunity cost of staying under-ranked is increasing right now.

email_copy.subject: EUR 188,014 sitting behind a rank bottleneck (9.02% IS; 91.0% lost to rank)
email_copy.hook:
I took a close look at your paid search account and the story is pretty clear: you’re not being held back by budget — you’re being held back by where you’re showing up (or not showing up) on non-brand searches that should be winnable.

Right now, you’re funding coverage with a daily budget of EUR 52,768, but most of the missed demand is happening because ad rank isn’t getting you into the auction often enough — even before budget is a factor.
why_now_bullets: In Germany insurance search, the typical advertiser is at 21.0% impression share — your account is at 9.02%.
Market spend is up 18.0% QoQ while your account is already losing 91.0% to rank — that gap tends to widen fast when auctions tighten.
Your account is losing 91.0% to rank while losing 0.0% to budget — meaning “more budget” won’t be the unlock until rank/quality is fixed.
email_copy.stat_sub: Unlocked by fixing ad rank (not raising budgets across the board)
email_copy.impact_line: The biggest lever here isn’t spend — it’s eligibility and position. With impression share at 9.02% and 91.0% lost to rank (0.0% lost to budget), you’re leaving qualified non-brand demand on the table that you could be competing for immediately once bids are concentrated on the right terms and low-value leakage stops dragging performance.
